entities.rationale: Rich and stable, but a nuclear target that imports half its energy and much of its food. Getting essentials from 24% to under 10% of income needs SI to cut health and care costs, which are rising as the population ages.

A nuclear-powered grid and a strong farm sector are strengths. Political instability, rising debt and being a nuclear power are the main risks, and essentials at 27% of income only fall below 10% with SI.
Severe water stress, a fragile grid, extreme violent crime and weak state capacity make a multi-year breakdown plausible. Deep poverty and inequality make near-free essentials unlikely even with SI.
Very safe and long-lived, but it imports 79% of its energy, is water-stressed, carries very high debt and is ageing fast. Abundance depends on SI offsetting the cost of caring for the elderly.

A third of people are already undernourished, and high climate vulnerability, heavy debt service and political volatility make a food or security breakdown the main risk. From such a low income, near-free essentials are a long shot.
Plenty of water and exportable energy, but armed groups, a high homicide rate and political instability make security the weak pillar.

War with North Korea, or a regional blockade of a country that imports 83% of its energy, is the main path to collapse. A strong state and tech base make it an early SI beneficiary, but extreme ageing and defence spending push costs up.
Peaceful and long-lived, but water stress is near the top of the scale and it imports most of its energy. Cheap solar and desalination help, yet near-free essentials still need SI.
A food and energy exporter far from the major wars, but repeated economic crises and weak institutions put health care and incomes at risk. Abundance needs SI plus decades of steady governance.
Rich in energy and water, stable and safe. The main risks are a US-Russia war spilling over and a global catastrophe.
Russia's ongoing invasion and its attacks on the power grid make a long loss of security or electricity the dominant risk. Abundance needs a lasting peace plus SI-driven rebuilding.

It depends almost entirely on desalination and imported food, and faces extreme heat, rivalry with Iran and the end of oil revenue. Cheap energy could make water nearly free, but high defence spending works against the cost test.
Stable, fast-growing and able to feed itself, but a frontline NATO state on Russia's border. High defence spending and rapid ageing make the near-free test hard.
Huge energy and food surpluses, stable institutions and distance from most wars. Drought, heat and a China-US conflict are the main local risks.
Very rich, with world-class flood defences that should handle sea-level rise through 2100. Its weak points are its low-lying land and its 88% dependence on imported energy.
Strong institutions, clean home-grown power, ample water and low debt. Baltic tensions with Russia are the main local risk.
The richest and most energy-secure country here, with essentials already at 20% of income and a huge sovereign wealth fund. Only a global catastrophe or a war with Russia plausibly breaks it.
